title: Functional Core, Imperative Shell

validation.research: Bernhardt's accessible original episode description establishes the named arrangement and its 2012-07-12 publication; his public Boundaries description supplies the value-boundary context. No subscription-video or transcript access is claimed. Seemann's primary articles distinguish an effectful callback from an already-read value and explain impure/pure/impure composition without requiring one enormous preload. Official Python documentation supports frozen-record limitations, CSV conversion and newline handling, and file context management. The replenishment scenario, Python code, and figures are original teaching material.
validation.python_examples: All three actual article blocks execute and print sku,units and pen,7 on separate lines. Checks verify constrained core imports and absence of direct I/O operations, repeated equal results without input changes, frozen item and proposal records, empty input, inclusive and adjacent thresholds, zero-unit suppression, over-target stock, identifier validation, duplicate rejection, invalid count types and values, target bounds, and input-order preservation. These focused checks do not constitute a general Python purity proof. Real CSV checks cover quoted identifiers, expected output, invalid later rows and malformed numeric input without opening or changing output, missing columns with rows, same-path rejection, missing input and invalid output paths, and handle closure. An instrumented real output stream fails after writing the header; the original exception propagates, the handle closes, and partial output remains, matching the stated non-atomic behavior. A fresh observation produces a fresh decision while the previously returned snapshot result stays unchanged.

example_limits: Single-threaded whole-batch CSV processing with an eager tuple of input records and local builders inside a value-based core. Frozen records contain only strings and integers; Python does not generally enforce purity. Results are proposals, not purchases or stock updates. Output is opened for ordinary replacement after complete parsing and validation; a write failure may leave partial output. No atomic file replacement, durable commit, inventory snapshot transaction, concurrency protection, or exactly-once effect execution is implemented. The shell requires the documented CSV columns and integer text counts.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
